analysis.analysis: A worker organization is composed with its founders and its tool, and its own stance on its data, the commitment the record quotes, is left out. The answer ends without an offer, at the expansion.
analysis.d: TURKOPTICON, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a worker-led advocacy organization and review system created in 2008 by Lilly Irani and M. Six Silberman.' The review tool for Mechanical Turk requesters (pay, fairness, speed, communication), its purpose against invisibility (unfair rejections, wage theft) and the expansion to data workers across industries. No closing offer. Seven cards: Turkopticon's own page, the CHI 2013 paper, the 2008–2015 lessons paper, a Reddit thread on the expansion, a LinkedIn post, a video.
analysis.d_full: TURKOPTICON, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a worker-led advocacy organization and review system created in 2008 by Lilly Irani and M. Six Silberman.' The review tool for Mechanical Turk requesters (pay, fairness, speed, communication), its purpose against invisibility (unfair rejections, wage theft) and the expansion to data workers across industries. No closing offer. Seven cards: Turkopticon's own page, the CHI 2013 paper, the 2008–2015 lessons paper, a Reddit thread on the expansion, a LinkedIn post, a video.
findings: THE ENTITY HELD. 2008, the founders, the requester reviews and the expansion to all data workers are the record's. 'Worker-led' is the record's present: a worker-run committee of Turk workers since 2019, maintained with volunteers from Tech Workers Coalition. Checked 2026-10-29 against the Labor Vector census record of the same day and the sources it saved.
THE METRICS. The record's FAQ gives the four ratings as communication, pay per hour, fairness of approvals and promptness; 'speed' is the composition's word for promptness.

WHAT TURKOPTICON SAYS IT IS NOT, UNSAID. The record's negative tags: not associated with Amazon; does not publish papers using its data, and use is not consent to being a research subject; its ratings are of requesters on Mechanical Turk, and it rates no platform. The composition says none of these and contradicts none.

REQUESTERS AS EMPLOYERS. The composition's 'review and rate employers ("requesters")' gives requesters a standing Turkopticon's FAQ withholds: 'While requesters are not employers in the legal sense, requesters are in a position of power over workers by virtue of making payment decisions'.
THE PRESENT WORK ABSENT. The working relationship with Amazon, the reinstatement system for suspended accounts and the mass-rejection campaign, the record's current findings, are not composed.

read.notes: Claim boundary present: a worker-led advocacy organization with its review system, workers rating requesters on pay, fairness, speed and communication (the four attributes). The composition calls requesters 'employers' ('review and rate employers ("requesters")'), where the FAQ states requesters 'are not employers in the legal sense'; recorded as a relabel of the parties, not of Turkopticon's own claim. Purpose present: the mission to organize data workers (the expansion beyond AMT), with transparency of worker-requester relations; building collective power and accountability are not named. Commitments absent: no-deletion for accountability, independence from Amazon, the research-data refusal and consent statement, the AGPL code are not carried. Lineage absent: the reputation-system model (Amazon Marketplace, eBay) is not named; 'employer reputation system' appears only on a card (SSRN). Framework absent: Tech Workers Coalition not named. Deposit chain absent: 'Originally launched as a browser extension and website' gives the tool's history, not a chain offered as a way to the work. The name atom's span is the composition's own link text; the word Turkopticon is the composition's, the URL is not read.
